items.title: Assign a variable
items.code:
SET score TO 0
SET name TO "Sam"
items.note: SET creates or updates a variable. Names are case-sensitive: Score and score are different.

items.title: Output
items.code: SEND "Hello " & name TO DISPLAY
items.note: Use & to join text and values into one line.

items.title: Input
items.code: RECEIVE age FROM (INTEGER) KEYBOARD
items.note: Types: INTEGER, REAL, STRING, BOOLEAN, CHARACTER. When RECEIVE runs, the console waits for you to type a value.

items.title: Comment
items.code: # This line is ignored
items.note: Everything after # on a line is a comment.

items.title: IF ... ELSE
items.code:
IF mark >= 50 THEN
    SEND "Pass" TO DISPLAY
ELSE
    SEND "Fail" TO DISPLAY
END IF
items.note: ELSE is optional. Every IF needs its own END IF.

items.title: More than two choices
items.code:
IF mark >= 70 THEN
    SET grade TO "A"
ELSE
    IF mark >= 50 THEN
        SET grade TO "B"
    ELSE
        SET grade TO "C"
    END IF
END IF
items.note: Nest a second IF inside ELSE.

items.title: FOR (count-controlled)
items.code:
FOR i FROM 1 TO 10 DO
    SEND i TO DISPLAY
END FOR
items.note: Add STEP 2 or STEP -1 after the end value to change the step.

items.title: WHILE (check first)
items.code:
SET count TO 0
WHILE count < 5 DO
    SET count TO count + 1
END WHILE
items.note: Checked before each pass, so the body may run zero times.

items.title: REPEAT ... UNTIL (check last)
items.code:
REPEAT
    RECEIVE guess FROM (INTEGER) KEYBOARD
UNTIL guess = 7
items.note: The body always runs at least once.

items.title: REPEAT n TIMES
items.code:
REPEAT 3 TIMES
    SEND "Hello" TO DISPLAY
END REPEAT

items.title: FOR EACH
items.code:
FOR EACH item FROM ["a", "b"] DO
    SEND item TO DISPLAY
END FOREACH
items.note: Visits every element of an array, or every character of a string.

items.title: Procedure
items.code:
PROCEDURE greet(name)
BEGIN PROCEDURE
    SEND "Hi " & name TO DISPLAY
END PROCEDURE

greet("Ava")
items.note: Call it on its own line. A procedure does not return a value.

items.title: Function
items.code:
FUNCTION square(n)
BEGIN FUNCTION
    RETURN n * n
END FUNCTION

SET area TO square(4)
items.note: A function must RETURN a value. Use it inside an expression.

items.title: Create and read
items.code:
SET scores TO [12, 18, 9]
SEND scores[0] TO DISPLAY
items.note: Indexes start at 0. The last index is LENGTH(scores) - 1.

items.title: Change an element
items.code: SET scores[1] TO 20

items.title: Loop over an array
items.code:
FOR i FROM 0 TO LENGTH(scores) - 1 DO
    SEND scores[i] TO DISPLAY
END FOR

items.title: 2D array
items.code:
SET grid TO [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
SEND grid[1][0] TO DISPLAY
items.note: Row first, then column. This shows 3.

items.title: Characters of a string
items.code:
SET word TO "code"
SEND word[0] TO DISPLAY
items.note: Strings index like arrays. LENGTH(word) is 4.

items.title: Arithmetic
items.code:
+  -  *  /  ^
7 DIV 2    is 3
7 MOD 2    is 1
items.note: / gives a real result. DIV is whole-number division, MOD the remainder.

items.title: Comparison
items.note: Use = to compare and <> for not equal. == and != are not Edexcel.

items.title: Logic and text
items.code:
AND  OR  NOT
"Total: " & total
items.note: & joins text. TRUE and FALSE are written in capitals.

items.title: LENGTH(x)
items.code: SET n TO LENGTH("hello")
items.note: Number of items in an array, or characters in a string.

items.title: RANDOM(n)
items.code: SET roll TO RANDOM(5) + 1
items.note: A random whole number from 0 to n inclusive.

items.title: INT(x) and STR(x)
items.code:
SET n TO INT("42")
SET s TO STR(3.5)
items.note: Conversion helpers supported by this IDE.

items.title: Declare
items.code:
DECLARE Total : INTEGER
DECLARE Name : STRING
items.note: Types: INTEGER, REAL, CHAR, STRING, BOOLEAN, DATE. Declare a variable before you use it.

items.title: Assign
items.code:
Total ← 0
Name ← "Sam"
items.note: Type <- for the arrow. Both work in this IDE.

items.title: Constant
items.code: CONSTANT VAT ← 0.2
items.note: 0478/2210 writes ←, 9618 writes =. Both are accepted.

items.title: Input and output
items.code:
OUTPUT "Enter your name"
INPUT Name
OUTPUT "Hello ", Name
items.note: OUTPUT joins the items you list with commas. No spaces are added.

items.title: Comment
items.code: // This line is ignored

items.title: IF ... ENDIF
items.code:
IF Mark >= 50
  THEN
    OUTPUT "Pass"
  ELSE
    OUTPUT "Fail"
ENDIF
items.note: THEN can go at the end of the IF line or on the next line. There is no ELSE IF: put another IF inside ELSE.

items.title: CASE OF
items.code:
CASE OF Choice
    1 : OUTPUT "Add"
    2 : OUTPUT "Delete"
    3 TO 5 : OUTPUT "Other"
    OTHERWISE : OUTPUT "Invalid"
ENDCASE
items.note: A branch can be a single value or a range with TO. OTHERWISE is optional and goes last.

items.title: FOR ... NEXT
items.code:
FOR Count ← 1 TO 10
    OUTPUT Count
NEXT Count
items.note: Add STEP 2 or STEP -1 after the end value.

items.title: WHILE ... ENDWHILE
items.code:
WHILE Total < 100 DO
    Total ← Total + 10
ENDWHILE
items.note: Checked first, so the body may run zero times. DO is optional (9618 leaves it out).

items.title: REPEAT ... UNTIL
items.code:
REPEAT
    INPUT Age
UNTIL Age >= 0 AND Age <= 120
items.note: The body always runs at least once.

items.title: 1D array
items.code:
DECLARE Scores : ARRAY[1:5] OF INTEGER
Scores[1] ← 12
items.note: You choose the bounds. Cambridge arrays usually start at 1.

items.title: 2D array
items.code:
DECLARE Grid : ARRAY[1:3, 1:4] OF CHAR
Grid[2, 3] ← 'X'
items.note: Row first, then column, separated by a comma.

items.title: Loop over an array
items.code:
Total ← 0
FOR i ← 1 TO 5
    Total ← Total + Scores[i]
NEXT i

items.title: Procedure
items.code:
PROCEDURE Greet(Name : STRING)
    OUTPUT "Hi ", Name
ENDPROCEDURE

CALL Greet("Ava")
items.note: Run a procedure with CALL.

items.title: Function
items.code:
FUNCTION Square(N : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    RETURN N * N
ENDFUNCTION

OUTPUT Square(4)
items.note: A function states its RETURNS type and gives back a value.

items.title: BYREF (9618)
items.code:
PROCEDURE AddOne(BYREF N : INTEGER)
    N ← N + 1
ENDPROCEDURE
items.note: BYREF changes the caller's variable. BYVAL (the default) works on a copy. BYREF applies to every parameter after it, until BYVAL.

items.title: Record type
items.code:
TYPE Book
    DECLARE Title : STRING
    DECLARE Pages : INTEGER
ENDTYPE

DECLARE B : Book
B.Title ← "Dune"

items.title: Text file
items.code:
OPENFILE "data.txt" FOR WRITE
WRITEFILE "data.txt", "first line"
CLOSEFILE "data.txt"
items.note: Modes: READ, WRITE, APPEND. Files live in memory until the program ends and show in Variables.

items.title: Read to the end
items.code:
OPENFILE "data.txt" FOR READ
WHILE NOT EOF("data.txt")
    READFILE "data.txt", Line
    OUTPUT Line
ENDWHILE
CLOSEFILE "data.txt"

items.title: Arithmetic
items.note: / always gives a REAL. 17 DIV 5 and 17 MOD 5 also work.

items.title: Comparison and logic
items.code:
=  <>  <  <=  >  >=
AND  OR  NOT
items.note: One = compares. <> means not equal.

items.title: Joining strings
items.code: FullName ← First & " " & Last
items.note: & joins STRING and CHAR values. Convert numbers with NUM_TO_STR.

items.title: LENGTH, UCASE, LCASE
items.code:
N ← LENGTH("Happy")
U ← UCASE("Happy")
L ← LCASE("Happy")
items.note: LENGTH counts characters. UCASE and LCASE change the case.

items.title: SUBSTRING
items.code: S ← SUBSTRING("Happy Days", 1, 5)
items.note: Start position (from 1) and length. Gives "Happy".

items.title: ROUND and RANDOM
items.code:
R ← ROUND(6.97354, 2)
X ← RANDOM()
items.note: ROUND to a number of decimal places. RANDOM gives a REAL from 0 to 1.

items.title: LEFT, RIGHT, MID
items.code:
L ← LEFT("ABCDEF", 3)
R ← RIGHT("ABCDEF", 2)
M ← MID("ABCDEF", 2, 3)
items.note: Gives "ABC", "EF" and "BCD".

items.title: TO_UPPER, TO_LOWER
items.code: U ← TO_UPPER("Hello")
items.note: Work on a STRING or CHAR. UCASE and LCASE work on a CHAR.

items.title: NUM_TO_STR, STR_TO_NUM, IS_NUM
items.code:
S ← NUM_TO_STR(3.5)
N ← STR_TO_NUM("42")
OK ← IS_NUM("42a")
items.note: Check text with IS_NUM before converting it.

items.title: ASC and CHR
items.code:
Code ← ASC('A')
C ← CHR(66)
items.note: Character codes: 65 and 'B'.

items.title: INT and RAND
items.code:
Whole ← INT(7.9)
Dice ← INT(RAND(6)) + 1
items.note: INT drops the decimal part. RAND(x) gives a REAL from 0 up to (not including) x.

items.title: Dates
items.code:
D ← SETDATE(25, 12, 2025)
OUTPUT DAY(D), MONTH(D), YEAR(D), DAYINDEX(D)
Today ← NOW()
items.note: DAYINDEX gives 1 for Sunday to 7 for Saturday.

items.title: Assign
items.code:
score = 0
name = "Sam"
items.note: Python creates the variable when you first assign it. Names are case-sensitive.

items.title: Output
items.code:
print("Hello", name)
print("Total: " + str(total))
print(f"Total: {total}")
items.note: print puts a space between items. + only joins text to text, so convert numbers with str() or use an f-string.

items.title: Input
items.code:
name = input("Name: ")
age = int(input("Age: "))
items.note: input() always gives text. Convert with int() or float(). When input() runs, the console waits for you to type a value and press Enter.

items.title: Comment
items.code: # This line is ignored

items.title: if / elif / else
items.note: Each line that starts a block ends with a colon. The block is indented by 4 spaces.

items.title: Comparison and logic
items.note: Use == to compare and = to assign.

items.title: for with range
items.code:
for i in range(1, 11):
    print(i)
items.note: range(1, 11) counts 1 to 10. The end value is not included.

items.title: for over a list
items.code:
for name in names:
    print(name)

items.title: while
items.note: Checked before each pass. break leaves the loop, continue skips to the next pass.

items.title: Function with return
items.note: A function without return gives back None.

items.title: Procedure-style function
Changing a global
items.code:
count = 0
def add():
    global count
    count += 1
items.note: Without global, assigning inside a function makes a new local variable.

items.title: Create and index
items.code:
scores = [12, 18, 9]
print(scores[0], scores[-1])
items.note: Indexes start at 0. -1 is the last item.

items.title: Change a list
items.code:
scores.append(20)
scores.insert(0, 5)
scores.remove(18)
last = scores.pop()

items.title: Slicing
items.code:
word = "Python"
print(word[0:3], word[::-1])
items.note: [start:end] stops before end. [::-1] reverses.

items.title: 2D list
items.note: Row first, then column. This shows 3.

items.title: String methods
items.code:
text.upper()  text.lower()  text.strip()
text.split(",")  ", ".join(items)
text.replace("a", "b")  len(text)
items.note: Strings cannot be changed in place. Methods return a new string.

items.title: Create and use
items.note: get() gives a default instead of a KeyError.

items.title: Loop over items
items.code:
for name, age in ages.items():
    print(name, age)

items.title: try / except
items.note: The except block runs when int() cannot convert the text.

items.title: Common built-ins
items.code:
len(x)  range(n)  int(x)  float(x)  str(x)
round(x, 2)  abs(x)  min(a)  max(a)  sum(a)
sorted(a)  ord("A")  chr(65)

items.title: random
items.code:
import random
dice = random.randint(1, 6)
pick = random.choice(names)
items.note: randint includes both ends.

items.title: math
items.code:
import math
print(math.sqrt(16), math.floor(2.7), math.pi)
items.note: The random, math and time modules are available.
